evidence: Majority pattern (~18 of 40 implementations): primary source file named 'active_inference.<ext>' (e.g., active_inference.lua, active_inference.nim, active_inference.zig, active_inference.erl, active_inference.ml, active_inference.odin, active_inference.rkt, active_inference.v, active_inference.cr, active_inference.f90, active_inference.asm, active_inference.pas)

Divergent naming islands: Python uses 'Student_Teacher.py', Java uses 'AntColony.java', Go uses 'GoLang_Agent.go'/'GoLang_Thing.go', Shell uses 'Active_Shellference.sh', C uses 'Active_Inference.c', Perl uses 'Perl_Agent.pl', Ruby uses 'active_inference_agent.rb'

PascalCase island: PHP=ActiveInferenceAgent.php, Swift=ActiveInferenceAgent.swift, TypeScript=src/ActiveInferenceAgent.ts, MATLAB=ActiveInferenceAgent.m, Cpp=src/ActiveInferenceAgent.cpp — five sibling modules use a distinct PascalCase convention

Rust is a structural style island: uses deep subdirectory nesting (RustConfig/, RustThings/, src/) with a unique dot-separated file naming scheme (Rust.config.rs, Rust.InferAnts.rs, Rust.Thing.rs, Rust.pseudo-pymdp_Ant_2.rs, Rust.metaconfig.rs) that appears nowhere else in the codebase

Julia directory is also a structural outlier: contains subdirectories (Category_Theory_Julia/, SideCar/, Visualization/) plus multiple loose .jl files (Clone_Julia_Repo.jl, Julia_InferAnts.jl, RxInfer.jl, RxInfer_Agent_Model.jl), unlike the flat single-source convention elsewhere

status_dashboard.sh check_language_status uses 'Go' as the case label (line 54) but show_implementations passes lang='Golang' — the case branch never fires, silently falling through to the default (run.sh as main_file), inconsistent with how run_all.sh references the same implementation as 'Golang:Golang'

Root-level mixes shell orchestrators (run_all.sh, status_dashboard.sh) with Python orchestrators (master_controller.py, benchmark_suite.py, config_manager.py, reporting_system.py) — two parallel control-plane conventions exist at the same level without documented rationale
All 40 language directories have a run.sh — this is a strong, uniform convention that holds without exception

strengths: Every single language directory (40/40) has a run.sh entry point — this uniform contract is respected without exception and makes the codebase navigable from run_all.sh

The dominant naming convention for primary source files is clear and widely followed: 'active_inference.<ext>' holds for roughly half the implementations, giving a new developer a strong starting expectation
Shell scripts share a consistent internal structure: shebang, set -e, color variable block, named functions, argument parsing — a developer reading any one run.sh can predict the shape of the others
Directory-level taxonomy (one directory per language, PascalCase directory names) is perfectly consistent across all 40+ entries
convention_outlier.issue_character: Convention drift is present at two layers simultaneously — source file naming (snake_case vs PascalCase vs domain-branded names) and directory structure (flat vs deeply nested) — with Rust and Julia functioning as fully isolated style islands that share almost no organizational DNA with the rest of the codebase.
convention_outlier.score_rationale: The codebase earns credit for a perfectly uniform run.sh convention and consistent directory naming. However, a developer trying to locate the primary source file for an unfamiliar language cannot predict the name: roughly half follow active_inference.<ext>, five use PascalCase ActiveInferenceAgent.<ext>, and a scatter of others (Student_Teacher.py, AntColony.java, GoLang_Agent.go, Perl_Agent.pl, Active_Shellference.sh) use entirely domain-branded names. Rust and Julia are structural islands with multi-level subdirectories and idiosyncratic file naming that a developer must re-learn from scratch. The status_dashboard.sh 'Go' vs 'Golang' mismatch is a low-impact functional bug rooted in the same naming drift. This lands at 68: a developer mostly knows where to look but encounters enough 'why is this different?' moments that they cannot rely on the pattern they learned from the last implementation.

issues.summary: Primary source file naming is inconsistent: ~18 use active_inference.<ext>, 5 use PascalCase ActiveInferenceAgent.<ext>, and 8+ use domain-branded names
evidence: active_inference.* is used in: Lua, Nim, Zig, Erlang, OCaml, Odin, Racket, V, Crystal, Fortran, Assembly, Pascal, JavaScript, R — the dominant pattern
ActiveInferenceAgent.* is used in: PHP, Swift, TypeScript, MATLAB, Cpp — a competing PascalCase pattern
Domain-branded names: Student_Teacher.py (Python), AntColony.java (Java), GoLang_Agent.go (Go), Active_Shellference.sh (Shell), Perl_Agent.pl (Perl) — each module invents its own naming
issues.suggestion: Standardize to 'active_inference.<ext>' as the canonical primary source file name across all implementations. For languages with strong idiomatic class-file conventions (Java, C#, Swift), document the exception explicitly in the top-level README. Rename the most divergent files: Student_Teacher.py -> active_inference.py, AntColony.java -> ActiveInference.java (or active_inference/Main.java), GoLang_Agent.go -> active_inference.go, Active_Shellference.sh -> active_inference.sh, Perl_Agent.pl -> active_inference.pl.

issues.summary: Rust directory uses a unique deep-nesting and dot-separated file naming scheme (Rust.config.rs, Rust.InferAnts.rs) shared by no other implementation
evidence: RustConfig/ and RustThings/ are organizational subdirectories that exist in no other language directory
Files use 'Rust.' as a namespace prefix (Rust.config.rs, Rust.InferAnts.rs) — a convention entirely absent from all other 39 implementations
RustConfig/ itself contains a further RustWorlds/ subdirectory, creating 3 levels of nesting vs the flat convention elsewhere
The canonical src/ directory (with main.rs, lib.rs, error.rs) coexists alongside these non-canonical directories, suggesting the Rust directory has grown without a unifying organizational plan
issues.suggestion: Consolidate the Rust directory to follow the codebase's flat convention: move logic from RustConfig/ and RustThings/ into src/ as proper Rust modules (src/config.rs, src/inference.rs, src/world.rs etc.), remove the 'Rust.' filename prefix (rust files already live in the Rust/ directory), and delete the RustConfig/ and RustThings/ directories. The src/main.rs + src/lib.rs layout already started correctly — extend it.

issues.summary: Julia directory contains multiple subdirectories (Category_Theory_Julia/, SideCar/, Visualization/) unlike the flat single-source convention used by all other implementations
evidence: Julia/ contains three named subdirectories (Category_Theory_Julia/, SideCar/, Visualization/) — no other language directory uses named subdirectories beyond the idiomatic src/, app/, or include/ seen in compiled languages
Julia/ also has 4 loose .jl files at top-level (Clone_Julia_Repo.jl, Julia_InferAnts.jl, RxInfer.jl, RxInfer_Agent_Model.jl) alongside the subdirectories, creating a mixed organizational model
The run.sh convention is respected but the directory content is far more elaborate than sibling language directories
issues.suggestion: Decide whether Julia is a single-demo implementation (like most siblings) or a multi-demo showcase; if the former, consolidate to one primary active_inference.jl and move extras to a reference/ or extras/ subdirectory with a note in README.md explaining the depth. If the latter, document the intentional deviation explicitly in Julia/README.md and Julia/run.sh.

issues.summary: status_dashboard.sh uses 'Go' as the case label for the Go language check but show_implementations passes lang='Golang', causing the case branch to never fire
evidence: Line 54: `"Go") main_file="$lang_dir/*.go" ;;` — the case label is 'Go'
show_implementations declares `["Concurrent"]="Golang:Golang Erlang:Erlang Elixir:Elixir"` — lang_info is parsed as lang='Golang', dir='Golang'
check_language_status is called as `check_language_status "Golang" "Golang"` so `$lang` is 'Golang', not 'Go' — the case branch silently falls through to default (`main_file="$lang_dir/run.sh"`)
run_all.sh consistently uses 'Golang:Golang', so the dashboard is the only location with this mismatch
issues.suggestion: On line 54 of status_dashboard.sh, change `"Go")` to `"Golang")` to match the name used in show_implementations and run_all.sh. This is a single-character edit: `"Golang") main_file="$lang_dir/*.go" ;;`

issues.summary: Root level mixes two parallel control-plane conventions: shell scripts (run_all.sh, status_dashboard.sh) and Python scripts (master_controller.py, benchmark_suite.py, config_manager.py, reporting_system.py) with overlapping responsibilities
evidence: master_controller.py.show_status() calls os.system(status_dashboard.sh) — the Python layer wraps the shell layer rather than the two being separate concerns
run_all.sh and master_controller.py both provide a 'run all implementations' entry point with no documented distinction of when to use which
status_dashboard.sh and reporting_system.py both generate status/health reports — overlapping scope
A developer arriving at the root is confronted with two entry-point conventions without guidance on which to use
issues.suggestion: Document the intended layering in the top-level README: either (a) shell scripts are the primary interface and Python scripts add analytics capabilities not expressible in shell, or (b) Python is the primary interface and shell scripts are lower-level primitives it calls. Add a 'Getting Started' section to README.md that points to the canonical entry point. If the Python layer simply wraps the shell layer with no added value, consolidate into the shell scripts.

root_causes: The codebase grew incrementally — each language implementation was likely added by different contributors or at different times, with no enforced naming template. The uniform run.sh convention suggests it was established early; the source file naming drifted as new implementations were added without a naming spec.
Rust and Julia directories appear to have been seeded from richer, pre-existing codebases rather than created fresh within this repository's conventions, explaining their structural divergence.

The dual shell/Python control plane at root suggests a refactoring-in-progress: shell scripts were the original interface and Python scripts were added later to provide richer functionality, but the old interface was never retired or clearly subordinated.
possible_false_positives: Language-idiomatic naming (e.g., AntColony.java follows Java class-file conventions, ActiveInferenceAgent.swift follows Swift type-file conventions) — these are intentional deviations mandated by the target language, not convention drift within the bash codebase itself
